How does evolution explain the process of plants and animals becoming poisonous?

Plants and animals that had the genes to be poisonous were avoided by predators. Therefore poisonous things survived better and propagated over many generations. If you mean how did they become poisonous in the first place, the answer is probably advantageous genetic mutation. However, I know that some insects are poisonous because of their diet.

If you mean how did they become poisonous in the first place, the answer is probably advantageous genetic mutation.

Ah, that's how I should have phrased it.

However, I know that some insects are poisonous because of their diet.

I would love to know just exactly how plants could create and internalize a poisonous substance. Probably something a pathology student would know.

I think I can at least partially answer you question!

There are many different types of poisons, each of which has different mechanisms through which unsuspecting organisms are killed.

For example, antibiotics/antimicrobials, which are produced naturally, for example from fungi (e.g. penicillin) or other microorganisms (e.g. streptomycin) are effective at killing bacteria (prokaryotic cells) while being relatively or completely harmless to other organisms (eukaryotic cells). This is because antimicrobials work by affecting structures that are unique to bacteria (e.g. their cell capsule or their smaller ribosomes). Since eukaryotic cells don't have these structures, the antimicrobials don't harm them.

Another type of poison is neurotoxins! Things like atropine, which can be found in nightshades, or botulinum toxin (botox), which is produced by a bacteria, work by blocking or overstimulating certain neurotransmitter pathways. Obviously, these substances would have no effect on plants or organisms that don't have neural pathways!

I guess one final consideration is where the toxin goes within an organism's body. Snake venom can be very deadly if it gets in your bloodstream (or another snake's bloodstream!), but poses no threat to the snake because it is stored in isolation in its venom sacs. Similarly, botox applied directly to the forehead will not have fatal complications as it only relaxes the muscles where it is injected.

Basically a random genetic mutation that caused a plant/animal to produce a chemical that harms others but not itself. That plant/animal had a distinct survival advantage, that plant would become inedible and succeed in reproduction much more likely than the non poisonous type. Rinse and repeat, and now the entire population is poisonous.

Not to be pedantic, but evolution does not explain the process. To be specific, natural selection explains how these features evolved. Remember, evolution is the process of allele distribution through a population. As for how a creature becomes poisonous, venomous, or toxic, /user/Boaz neatly addressed why these traits were advantageous in the process of natural selection, which in turn explains how these alleles were distributed though out a population of plants and animals. Week 3 of tavern bra- OH SHIT SPIDERS OH GOD OH GOD OH NO! BURN IT ALL TO THE GROUND!

Premise: Pick a class and you will get a deck full of webspinners and random class cards. Similar to the hunter challenge from Naxx.

Picking a class:

Tier 1 classes:

  • Rogue: Mana efficient hero power. Many spells that are great with/against webspinners e.g. Shiv, FoK, Oil, Bladeflurry, Coldblood.
  • Mage: Tons of useful spells e.g. Arcane Explosion, Arcane Missiles, Cone of Cold, Flamestrike, Blizzard.
  • Hunter: Fantastic hero power for closing out games. Great synergy with webspinners e.g. Kill Command, Unleash, Snake Trap, Hunter's Mark, Explosive trap.

Tier 2:

  • Druid: Decent hero power, Swipe is pretty good.
  • Warrior: Whirlwind, Execute and Revenge aren't half bad.
  • Shaman: Earthshock is cool, I guess. You will lose out on too much tempo if you spend mana on totems.
  • Paladin: Equality can come in handy.
  • Priest: Shadow madness, Velen's and Holy Nova are sweet, but your hero power won't kick in until it's too late.

Tier 3:

  • Warlock: Sacrificial Pact, Sense Demons, Demonwrath, Demonfire, and Demonheart are close to useless. Mortal coil is pretty sweet though.

Mulligan:

Mulligan for spells, spells are rare and valuable. Worst case you'll just get back spiders.

Playing it out:

It's all about tempo and board control.

Don't just vomit webspinners, use them to fill out your curve. Play your turns as if they don't exist and then use any spare mana at the end of your turn to spam spiders. This also means DO NOT COIN OUT WEBSPINNERS, that kinda shit will lose you the game. There are exceptions like Hyena, Buzzard and Rhino, so up to your judgement.

Don't feel bad if ya lose, this week's brawl is quite heavy on the RNG, but playing it out right will increase your win rate.
